- When sentiment turns negative and news volume drops to 0, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — cap forecast at 1–2 standard deviations above recent high.
- If sentiment shows strong negative change (e.g., -1.00) followed by zero news, model underreacts — adjust downward by 2–5% to match true mean reversion.
- When sentiment is neutral or weak (0.00) and news is low, model overestimates volatility — reduce forecast variance by 15–30%.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is positive — apply 3–5% downward bias for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is positive but news volume is low, model tends to overestimate price — apply 2–4% downward correction.
- When sentiment is positive and news volume is high, model often underestimates upside — add 1–3% upward bias to forecast.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is weak and recent price is falling — apply 1–3% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
